entry.title: Gradient of the Green’s function
entry.content:
For an observation vector \(\vec r =x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}\) and a source vector on \(\vec r^\prime=x^\prime\hat{i} + z^\prime\hat{i} + z^\prime\hat{k}\), the Green’s function for the homogeneous electromagnetic scattering problems is

egin{equation} \label{start_eq} g(\vec r - \vec r^\prime)= rac{e^{ikR}}{4\pi R}, \end{equation}

where the difference vector is \(\vec R = \vec r-\vec r^\prime\) and its length is \(R = \|\vec R\|\). The gradient operator in the cartesian coordinates is

\[ abla = rac{\partial }{\partial x}\hat{\imath} + rac{\partial }{\partial y}\hat{\jmath} + rac{\partial }{\partial k}\hat{z}.\]

The gradient of the Green’s function is

\[ abla g= rac{1}{4\pi R} abla e^{ikR} + e^{ikR} abla rac{1}{4\pi R}\]

by the product rule. Using the differentiation of exponential and the quotient rule, the gradient is

\[ abla g = rac{1}{4\pi R}\cdot ik\cdot e^{ikR}\cdot abla R + e^{ikR}\cdot rac{1}{4\pi}\cdot rac{-1}{R^2}\cdot abla{R}\]

and the formula is further organized as

\[ abla{g}= rac{e^{ikR}}{4\pi R}\cdot ik\cdot abla{R} - rac{e^{ikR}}{4\pi R}\cdot rac{1}{R} abla{R}\]

and

\[ abla{g}= rac{ikR}{4\pi R}\Big(ik- rac{1}{R} \Big) abla{R}.\]

For the defined \(\vec r\) and \(\vec r^\prime\), the difference vector is written explicitly

\[R = \sqrt{(x-x^\prime)^2 + (y-y^\prime)^2 + (z-z^\prime)^2}.\]

The gradient of \(R\) is

\[ abla{R}= rac{\partial{R}}{\partial x}\hat{i}+ rac{\partial{R}}{\partial y}\hat{j} + rac{\partial{R}}{\partial z}\hat{k}.\]

The partial derivative of the \(x\) component is

\[ rac{\partial R}{\partial x} = rac{1}{2} rac{2\cdot rac{\partial(x-x^\prime)}{\partial{x}}\cdot(x -x^\prime)}{\sqrt{(x-x^\prime)^2 + (y-y^\prime)^2 + (z-z^\prime)^2}}.\]

The organization of the equation gives

\[ rac{\partial R}{\partial x}= rac{x-x^\prime}{R}.\]

The result for the differentiation of the \(x\) component also defines the partial component of the \(y\) and \(z\) components and the gradient of the distance \(R\) is

\[ abla R= rac{x-x^\prime}{R}\hat{i} + rac{y-y^\prime}{R}\hat{j} + rac{z-z^\prime}{R}\hat{k},\]

which takes the form

\[ abla R = rac{\vec r - \vec r^\prime}{R}= rac{\vec R}{R}.\]

Therefore, the unit distance vector is \(\hat R = rac{\vec R}{R}= abla R\). The gradient of the Green’s function is

\[ abla g=\Big(ik - rac{1}{R}\Big) rac{e^{ikR}}{4\pi R}\hat{R}.\]

Finally, after the simplifications, the gradient of the Green’s function is

\[ abla{g(\vec r - \vec r^\prime)}=\Big(ik- rac{1}{|\vec r - \vec r^\prime|}\Big) rac{\vec r - \vec r^\prime}{|\vec r - \vec r^\prime|}g(\vec r - \vec r^\prime).\]
